title: Board of Medicine statement of the pharmacist qualifications
rule_summary: Under 243 CMR 2.12(2), in accordance with M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2(b), to qualify to enter into a collaborative practice agreement a pharmacist must: (a) hold a current unrestricted license in good standing to practice pharmacy in the Commonwealth and currently be engaged in pharmacy practice in the Commonwealth; (b) agree to maintain at least $1,000,000 (per occurrence) of professional liability insurance during the term of the agreement which specifically covers drug therapy management; (c) HAVE EARNED A DOCTOR OF PHARMACY DEGREE OR HAVE COMPLETED FIVE YEARS OF EXPERIENCE as a licensed pharmacist; (d) agree to devote a portion of the practice to the defined drug therapy area that the pharmacist shall co-manage; (e) agree to complete, in each year of the term of the agreement, at least five additional contact hours OR 0.5 CONTINUING EDUCATION UNITS of Board of Registration in Pharmacy approved continuing education that address areas of practice generally related to the particular collaborative practice agreement; and (f) if prescriptive practices are included in the agreement, agree to maintain a current controlled substance registration issued by the Department during the term of the agreement, pursuant to M.G.L. c. 94C, ss. 7 and 9 and 105 CMR 700.000.
exam_relevance: Tests the divergence between the two boards on the same statutory element: 243 CMR 2.12(2)(c) states the doctor of pharmacy degree as a free-standing alternative while 247 CMR 16.02(1)(c) confines it to an agreement entered on or before June 30, 2017, and 243 CMR 2.12(2)(e) carries a 0.5 continuing education unit alternative that 247 CMR 16.02(1)(e) does not.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Medicine regulations

numeric_facts.conditions: per occurrence, maintained during the term of the agreement, specifically covering drug therapy management

in each year of the term of the agreement, with 0.5 continuing education units stated as an alternative, addressing areas of practice generally related to the particular collaborative practice agreement

common_confusions: 243 CMR 2.12(2) is the Board of Registration in Medicine's list; 243 CMR 2.12(1) separately requires an authorized pharmacist to meet 247 CMR 16.02, which states the credential element more narrowly.
verification_notes: Read in the current official publication of 243 CMR 2.00 at the Board of Registration in Medicine download link on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule rather than by changing an existing record, so that no released adjudication is disturbed.
